relevance_note: The paper describes eight TNFAIP3 variant carriers first-hand: "Herein, we report eight patients with HA20 from three unrelated families in China."
method_note: Read the full paper by hand; a Python script assembled the JSON from values I chose, and built Table 1 spans by cutting each Table 1 row at the needed column (output checked against the table; every span verified verbatim by script). Table 1 has patients as rows but labels them only by pedigree number (1/2/3); rows were matched to people as follows: pedigree-1 row with onset 18 / diagnosis 28 = P1; the three identical pedigree-1 rows (F, UN, >18) = mother IV:14 and sisters V:22, V:26 (the order cannot be told apart, but the rows are identical); pedigree-2 row onset 9 = the daughter IV:1, onset 15 = P2; pedigree-3 M row = P3, F row onset 8 = the daughter IV:1. The table legend defines '-' as negative, so '–' cells were treated as explicit negatives (not as missing). Labels: probands use the paper's P1/P2/P3; the two daughters are both 'IV:1' in different families, so their labels are the verbatim phrases 'her 13-year-old daughter (IV:1)' (Family 2) and 'his 10-year-old daughter (IV:1)' (Family 3). Family 2 cousins III:3/III:4 are distinct from P3 (III:3 in Family 3). Relatives without variant data but with clinical statements (F1 father IV:13 'had no symptoms'; F1 cousin V:10 and 'her son' VI:7 with G6PD deficiency; F2 aunt II:3 and cousins III:3, III:4, who refused testing; F3 mother II:4 and late maternal grandmother I:4) are their own rows without variant rows. Family 1 grandparents III:2/III:3 (stated to be cousins) were not given rows (no clinical or genetic data), and consanguinity was left 'not reported' for everyone because the paper does not state parental consanguinity for any individual. CONTRADICTIONS: (1) P1 genital ulcers: text 'She had recurrent oral and genital ulcers from the age of 22' and discussion 'including oral and genital ulcers' vs Table 1 Genital ulcers '–' (checklist set to not reported). (2) P2 fever: text 'without recurrent fever' vs Table 1 Fever '+' (checklist not reported). (3) Family 2 daughter fever: text 'recurrent fever ... since the age of nine' vs Table 1 Fever '–' (checklist not reported); (2) and (3) look like the fever cells are swapped between the two Family 2 rows. (4) P3 autoantibodies: positive anti-TG/anti-TPO (text and table) vs 'Blood tests for CBC, biochemistry panel, and autoantibodies were all normal' (checklist not reported). (5) P3 onset: text 'recurrent oral ulcers since the age of 10' vs Table 1 age at onset 15; the individual onset field uses the text value. (6) A547T pathogenicity: abstract 'validated to be pathogenic' vs discussion 'the accurate pathogenic significance of A547T was indeed unknown'; both quoted. (7) c.1906+2T>G is given as '(exon 7)' in Table 1 but discussed as an intron 7 splice-site variant in the text. Other notes: P3's Table 1 Genital ulcers '+' was recorded as observed although the text describes only a 'perianal ulcer with an abscess' (the abstract's 'perianal ulcer (3/8)' matches the three '+' genital-ulcer cells). P3's Henoch-Schonlein purpura was mapped to the vasculitis checklist item; Table 1 Skin lesions for P3 is '–' and was kept as excluded. P1's 'joint pain ... without joint swelling' sits beside Table 1 Arthritis '+'; checklist 'arthritis or arthralgia' is observed either way. Ages in the case narratives (28-, 35-, 13-, 40-, 10-year-old) were put in age at last evaluation; for the probands they equal the Table 1 age at diagnosis, and P1 was followed for more than a year afterwards. Inheritance of TNFAIP3 variants was left 'not reported' (the paper does not state origin, though P1's mother and the daughters' proband parents carry the same variants; recorded in parental_testing_statement). Zygosity of A547T in P1's mother and sisters is not stated for them individually, so left 'not reported'. The father's 'no symptoms' was recorded as one excluded feature only; checklist items were not excluded from it. P2's moderate anemia was not counted as 'cytopenia (autoimmune)' because no autoimmune cause is stated. A NOD2 variant (stated as paternal) and a G6PD variant were recorded for P1 only; no variant row was made for the father. The literature review (126 patients, 35 articles) gives no patient-level table, so no review individuals were extracted. Column headers: Table 1 columns are Pedigree | TNFAIP3 variations (NM_006290) | Gender | Age at onset | Age at diagnosis | Oral ulcers | Genital ulcers | Skin lesions | Gastrointestinal lesions | Fever | Arthritis | Uveitis | Auto-Ab.
